claims.statement: Polish providers publicly list paid home sleep-apnea services, including 200 PLN screening, 400 PLN type-III home polygraphy, and a separate 500 PLN home test offer.
Self-paying patients demonstrably face a priced diagnostic event; the willingness of clinics to substitute a wholesale external capacity service is not evidenced.
A plausible control path is purchased or leased device capacity plus a formal medical-services agreement and clinic contracts; none has been obtained and the founder cannot supply clinical judgment.
A clinic's separate monthly CPAP-monitoring price suggests a possible downstream recurring workflow, but it does not prove demand for outsourced monitoring.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Clinic owner or diagnostic-service lead; patient for direct-pay arrangements
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Faster local turnaround, low failure rates, transparent service levels, and no clinic capex must offset limited clinical control
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Clinics own their patient relationships; the proposed capacity contract does not yet exist
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Direct clinic contract, physician referral, or CPAP provider partnership

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Clinic sales, medical partner onboarding, and referral fees where lawful
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Patient prepayment or monthly clinic invoicing while equipment capital is paid upfront
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Depends primarily on device utilization, failure rate, and specialist cost; no unit economics are established
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Patient instruction, device handoff, technical review, scheduling, and clinic support
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Device maintenance, medical and product liability, GDPR health-data controls, clinical governance, and insurance
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Target 300-450 PLN wholesale or 450-650 PLN retail per adequate interpreted study
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Physician interpretation, courier, consumables, cleaning, payment fees, and failed-study repeats

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Hospitals, private chains, CPAP vendors, telemedicine providers, and clinics can own devices or contract existing diagnostic labs
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: A technically adequate, physician-reviewed home study is paid; measurable losses are idle devices, failed recordings, repeated visits, and delayed report turnaround
commercial_mechanics.payer: Private clinic under wholesale capacity terms or self-paying patient under a clinic-supervised pathway
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Clinic waitlist, device failure, seasonal demand spike, new sleep-service launch, or patient preference for home testing
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Each completed referral, with quarterly or annual clinic capacity renewal

contrary_evidence: Existing clinics already own or access home-test workflows and can add devices directly.
Published consumer prices are low relative to courier, specialist, support, cleaning, repeat-test, and acquisition costs.
A device pool without referral density suffers poor utilization.

critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Lease replaceable devices from another compliant supplier and provide logistics only to clinics retaining interpretation
critical_control_point.current_owner: Unselected medical-device distributors, lessors, or clinics
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Clinics own their patient relationships; the proposed capacity contract does not yet exist
critical_control_point.duration: Asset useful life after purchase; no asset has been acquired
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder has relevant analytical interest but no medical license, clinic contract, device ownership, or right to rely on a medical-student relationship for clinical work
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Device owner plus contracted medical partner; neither is secured
critical_control_point.renewal: Device maintenance and medical-services terms require recurring renewal
critical_control_point.subject: Fleet of compliant home sleep-study devices and booking slots

economics.acquisition_route: Contracts with small private clinics and CPAP or dental-sleep referral partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Conditional path: a dense multi-city network completing 2,000 studies monthly at 100 PLN contribution yields 2.4m PLN annual contribution before overhead; a defensible clinic network might exceed 5m PLN in value, but regulation, utilization, and margins are unknown
economics.founder_time: A five-to-ten-device pilot could fit 3-5 hours daily only with outsourced courier and licensed interpretation
economics.gross_margin_basis: Per-study price less interpretation, delivery, consumables, cleaning, failed-study repeats, support, and device depreciation
economics.payback: Target device payback within 80-150 completed studies depending on acquisition and specialist costs; wholly unvalidated
economics.pricing: Discovery hypothesis: 300-450 PLN wholesale or 450-650 PLN retail per adequate physician-reviewed study
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat comes from clinic referral volume, not usually the same patient; capacity contracts may renew quarterly

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Device utilization, repeat-failure, patient-instruction, and turnaround data improve routing and reduce unusable studies
fingerprint.customer: Small private pulmonology, ENT, cardiology, obesity, and dental-sleep clinics in Poland
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Clinic contracts and referral pathways rather than consumer influencer marketing
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owned or leased diagnostic-device capacity, patient logistics, quality control, and specialist-report coordination sold per completed study
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The clinic or patient pays when a technically adequate study and physician-reviewed report are completed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A clinician wants a home sleep study but lacks an available device, trained handoff workflow, or reliable patient-return logistics

founder_fit: Sleep and physiological time-series quality control align with neuroscience and quantified-self interests
Device-utilization and failure-rate optimization fit data-science skills
Clinic-channel distribution avoids an on-camera consumer-health brand
A bounded device pool can test operations within roughly 100k PLN, although clinical work must remain with licensed professionals
risks: False negatives, poor recordings, or delayed escalation can harm patients
Health-data handling raises severe privacy and security requirements
Medical labor or device downtime can destroy unit economics
The founder's lack of clinical credentials prevents independent operation of the medical pathway

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: per study utilization of a pooled home diagnostic device fleet
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: proposed owned or leased home sleep study device capacity
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: licensed physician oversight and interpretation plus trained quality review

structure.commercial_archetype: Diagnostic asset-pool operator paid per completed study
structure.control_point: The proposed owned or leased fleet and booking capacity
structure.critical_dependency: Licensed clinicians and compliant devices for ordering, interpretation, and medical accountability

thesis: Observed purchasing and pricing signal: Polish providers publicly charge roughly 200-500 PLN for home sleep-apnea screening or type-III polygraphy, and one clinic separately prices monthly CPAP monitoring. Operate a small pool of compliant home-test devices, courier logistics, patient instructions, data-quality checks, and contracted physician interpretation for clinics that want test capacity without buying and scheduling their own fleet.
title: Home Sleep-Diagnostic Device Pool for Private Clinics
uncertainties: Applicable Polish medical-device, healthcare-entity, ordering, and telemedicine requirements
Device purchase or lease price, useful life, cleaning protocol, and consumable cost
Share of studies requiring repeats and physician-review cost
Clinic willingness to outsource capacity while retaining medical responsibility
